routes.label: Express each perpendicular as a fraction of AF

question:
\(ABCD\) is a rectangle (see the accompanying diagram) with \(P\) any point on \(\overline{AB}.\) \(PS\perp BD\) and \(PR\perp AC.\) \(AF\perp BD\) and \(PQ\perp AF.\) Then \(PR+PS\) is equal to:

[Figure 1](figures/1958_AMC_12_Q47_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
[Figure 1](figures/1958_AMC_12_Q47_question_fig1.svg)

Let \(E\) be the intersection of the diagonals, as labeled. A rectangle has equal diagonals that bisect each other, so \(AE=BE>0\). This makes an area comparison useful: \(PR\) and \(PS\) are heights to the equal bases \(AE\) and \(BE\).

Write \([XYZ]\) for the area of triangle \(XYZ\). Since \(P\) lies on \(AB\), segment \(EP\) divides triangle \(AEB\) into triangles \(AEP\) and \(PEB\). Also, \(AF\) is the height from \(A\) to the line containing \(BE\). Therefore
\[
\frac12 BE\cdot AF
=[AEB]
=[AEP]+[PEB]
=\frac12 AE\cdot PR+\frac12 BE\cdot PS.
\]
Using \(AE=BE\) and dividing by the positive number \(BE/2\) gives
\[
AF=PR+PS.
\]
The area equation also holds at \(P=A\) or \(P=B\), when one smaller triangle has zero area. Thus the answer is \(\boxed{AF}\), choice \(\boxed{D}\).

solutionMethods.explanation:
Let \(E=AC\cap BD\). The diagonals of a rectangle are equal and bisect each other, so \(AE=BE\). Thus triangle \(AEB\) is isosceles, giving
\[
\angle BAE=\angle ABE.
\]
These equal angles let us compare the perpendiculars with \(AF\) using right triangles.

If \(P\ne A\), triangles \(APR\) and \(BAF\) are similar: both are right triangles, and \(\angle PAR=\angle ABF\). Matching their hypotenuses and opposite legs gives
\[
\frac{PR}{AF}=\frac{AP}{AB}.
\]
This equality also holds when \(P=A\), since then \(PR=AP=0\).

If \(P\ne B\), right triangles \(BPS\) and \(BAF\) share their angle at \(B\), so
\[
\frac{PS}{AF}=\frac{PB}{AB}.
\]
This equality also holds when \(P=B\), since then \(PS=PB=0\). The denominators \(AF\) and \(AB\) are positive because the rectangle is nondegenerate.

Adding the two equalities and using \(AP+PB=AB\), we obtain
\[
PR+PS=AF\left(\frac{AP+PB}{AB}\right)=AF.
\]
Hence the answer is \(\boxed{AF}\), choice \(\boxed{D}\).
